stages.title: Language sounds and pronunciation
stages.hook: Say "mā", "má", "mǎ", "mà". The sounds look the same, but is the tune the same?
explain: Standard Mandarin (Pǔtōnghuà) is a tone language. The same syllable said with a different pitch tune is a different word. There are four tones and a light neutral tone: first tone is high and flat (mā), second rises (má), third dips down and up (mǎ), fourth falls sharply (mà).

Pinyin is the spelling system that writes Mandarin sounds with the Latin alphabet. Tone marks sit on the vowel. Some sounds are new to English speakers, such as x, q, zh and ü. Say each one slowly and listen to the tune.
stages.mnemonic: Tones are a roller coaster: flat road, going up, down and up, then a drop.

gq.q: How many tones does Standard Mandarin have, not counting the neutral tone?
gq.why: There are four main tones plus a light neutral tone.

gq.q: In pinyin, which word has the falling tone, like a firm "No!"?
gq.why: The fourth tone falls sharply and is marked with a falling accent.

panel.q: A learner says "mǎ" (horse) but uses a high flat tune and so says "mā". What is the problem?
o: Nothing, because tone is only for singing
The pinyin spelling has too many letters
Chinese has no difference between these sounds
panel.why: Tone is part of the word. Changing the tone changes the word, so the listener may hear "mum" instead of "horse".

panel.q: What is pinyin?
o: The only way Chinese people write every day
A Latin-letter spelling for Mandarin sounds
panel.why: Pinyin is a way to write Mandarin sounds with Latin letters. It is not the Chinese writing system itself.

panel.q: Why do dictionaries put tone marks on pinyin?
o: Many words differ only by tone
Tone marks only show the stressed English syllable
Tone marks are decorations with no use
They show how many strokes a character has
panel.why: Without tone marks, many different words look the same, so the tone helps show the meaning.

teach.topic: How the four tones work in Mandarin
teach.model: Mandarin words have a pitch tune as well as consonants and vowels. Four tunes exist: high flat, rising, dipping, and falling. For example, mā is mum and mǎ is horse. If you change the tune you change the word.

points.ask: What is a tone?
How many tones are there?
Can you give me an example where the tone changes the meaning?

trip.prompt: Listen to a short sample on the page. Can you hear the pitch go up or down?

stages.title: Alphabet, script or basic characters
stages.hook: Look at 山. Does it remind you of something? Chinese characters began as little pictures.
explain: Chinese is written with characters (hànzì). Each character is one syllable and usually carries a meaning. Many early characters were pictures: 山 is a mountain with three peaks, 日 is the sun, 月 is the moon, and 人 is a person walking.

Characters are built from smaller parts called radicals. The water radical 氵 appears in many words about liquids, and 口 (mouth) is in words about speaking or eating. Characters are written stroke by stroke, usually from top to bottom and from left to right.

Mainland China, Singapore and Malaysia usually use simplified characters, which have fewer strokes. Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau mostly use traditional characters. Standard Mandarin is only one Chinese language variety: Cantonese, Shanghainese and Hokkien are others. They share a writing tradition but are spoken differently.
stages.mnemonic: Draw the picture: 山 has three peaks, 日 is a window with the sun, 口 is an open mouth.
sentences: There is a lot of water.

gq.q: Which is true about the character 山?
o: It is built only from sounds and has no meaning
It is a picture of a mountain
It means water and shows a river with waves
It is a Latin letter used in pinyin spelling
gq.why: It began as a picture of a mountain with peaks.

gq.q: Which writing do people in Taiwan mostly use?
gq.why: Taiwan mostly uses traditional characters, while mainland China uses simplified ones.

panel.q: A friend says Chinese is one spoken language. What is a better description?
o: They are all just accents of English
A family of related varieties with a shared writing tradition
panel.why: Chinese has many varieties, such as Mandarin, Cantonese and Hokkien, which are often not mutually understandable when spoken.

panel.q: Why are radicals useful when learning characters?
o: They give clues about meaning and help with dictionaries
They tell you which tone to use and how to say each word aloud
They are used only in traditional characters, never in simplified
They are random extra lines with no link to any meaning
panel.why: Radicals often hint at meaning or sound, so they help you remember and look up characters.

panel.q: Why was simplification of characters introduced in mainland China?
o: To make Chinese into a Latin alphabet language
To make writing easier and reduce strokes
panel.why: Fewer strokes make characters faster to learn and write, to help literacy.

teach.model: A Chinese character is a written symbol for a syllable with a meaning. Many started as pictures, like 山 for mountain. Characters are made from parts called radicals, and written in a set stroke order.

points.ask: What is a Chinese character?
Where did characters come from?
What are they made from?

trip.prompt: Find the page section on simplified and traditional characters. Name one place that uses each.

stages.title: Greetings and introductions
stages.hook: How do you say hello to a teacher and to a friend in China? Is it the same?
explain: The most common greeting is 你好 (nǐ hǎo), meaning hello. For an older person or in polite speech, use 您好 (nín hǎo). 您 is the polite form of "you". In the morning say 早上好 (zǎoshang hǎo), and in the evening 晚上好.
To say thank you, say 谢谢 (xièxie). The reply is 不客气 (bú kèqi), which means "you are welcome". To say sorry, say 对不起 (duìbuqǐ). To say goodbye, say 再见 (zàijiàn).
To introduce yourself, say 我叫 (wǒ jiào) plus your name. To ask a name, say 你叫什么名字？(nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?). Chinese names put the family name first, then the given name.
stages.mnemonic: Nǐ hǎo is "you good": a greeting that wishes someone well.

gq.q: Which greeting is more polite when speaking to an elderly teacher?
gq.why: 您 is the polite "you" and is used for elders and in formal situations.

gq.q: Someone says 谢谢. What is a natural reply?

panel.q: In the name 王小明, which part is the family name?
panel.why: Chinese names put the family name first. 王 (Wáng) is the family name and 小明 is the given name.

panel.q: Why would a student say 您好 to a new principal but 你好 to a classmate?
o: The classmate is older, so the greeting has to change
Respect and closeness change the form of "you"
There is no difference, since both greetings mean exactly the same
您 is only used in writing and is never said aloud
panel.why: Mandarin marks respect with the polite pronoun 您.

panel.q: What does the 好 in 你好 and 早上好 add?
panel.why: 好 means good, so these greetings wish someone well.

teach.topic: Greeting and introducing yourself in Mandarin
teach.model: You can greet someone with 你好, or 您好 to be polite. To say your name, say 我叫 and then your name. In China the family name comes first, so Wang Xiaoming is the family name Wang and the given name Xiaoming.

points.ask: How do I say hello?
How do I say my name?
Which name goes first in Chinese?

trip.prompt: Look at how Chinese names are ordered and find one famous person from a Chinese-speaking place.

stages.title: Numbers and counting
stages.hook: Show 6 with one hand. In China, people have special hand signs for numbers. Can you count to ten in Chinese?
explain: Chinese numbers are very regular. 一 yī, 二 èr, 三 sān, 四 sì, 五 wǔ, 六 liù, 七 qī, 八 bā, 九 jiǔ, 十 shí. After ten you just build: 十一 is 11, 二十 is 20, and 二十三 is 23.

The first three numbers are easy to write: 一 is one line, 二 is two lines, 三 is three lines. To say how many things there are, you put a measure word between the number and the noun, such as 三个苹果 (three apples).
The number 二 is used for counting, but 两 (liǎng) is used before measure words: 两个人 means two people. The number 八 is considered lucky because it sounds like the word for getting rich.
stages.mnemonic: 一, 二, 三 are one, two, three lines. Then count the sounds: yī, èr, sān, sì, wǔ.

gq.q: How do you write 12 in Chinese?
gq.why: Chinese builds numbers from ten plus one: 十二.

gq.q: Which is the correct way to say "two people"?
gq.why: Before a measure word, Mandarin normally uses 两.

panel.q: What is 二十三?
panel.why: 二十 is twenty and 三 is three, so it is 23.

panel.q: Why is the number 8 popular in Chinese culture?
o: It looks like a snake, which is a lucky animal in China
It is the smallest number, so people see it as the best
Its sound is like a word for prosperity
It is the first number you say when you start counting
panel.why: 八 (bā) sounds like 发 (fā), "to get rich", so it is seen as lucky.

panel.q: Why do you say 三个苹果 and not 三苹果?
o: Numbers cannot be used with fruit
panel.why: Mandarin needs a measure word between a number and a noun.

teach.model: The numbers one to ten are yī, èr, sān, sì, wǔ, liù, qī, bā, jiǔ, shí. Larger numbers are built by combining them, so twelve is ten plus two. When counting things you add a measure word, like three apples.

points.ask: Can you say some numbers?
How do I make bigger numbers?
What goes between the number and the thing?

trip.prompt: Find how to write numbers 1 to 10 and spot the three that are just lines.

stages.title: Colours and shapes
stages.hook: What colour is the sky? What shape is the moon? Let us name them in Chinese.
explain: Many colour words end in 色 (sè), which means colour: 红色 (red), 黄色 (yellow), 蓝色 (blue), 绿色 (green), 白色 (white) and 黑色 (black). Red is a very lucky colour in China and is used for festivals and weddings.
Shapes end with 形 (xíng), meaning shape: 圆形 is a circle and 方形 is a square. A common sentence pattern is "thing + 是 + colour + 的": 苹果是红色的 means the apple is red.
Adjectives like 大 and 圆 can describe things without 是. You say 月亮很圆 (the moon is round). The word 很 often sits before an adjective, even when it does not really mean "very".
stages.mnemonic: Red 红, yellow 黄, blue 蓝, green 绿: colour words like 色 at the end.

gq.q: Which character at the end of 红色 means "colour"?
gq.why: 色 means colour and appears in many colour words.

gq.q: How do you say "a square" in Chinese?
gq.why: 形 means shape, and 方形 is a square.

panel.q: Why might a wedding in China use lots of red?
o: Red is the only colour available
Red is the colour of rain
panel.why: Red is associated with luck and happiness in Chinese culture.

panel.q: Which sentence means "The leaf is green"?
panel.why: Use thing + 是 + colour + 的.

panel.q: In 月亮很圆, what does 很 do?
o: It links the subject to the adjective
It makes the adjective plural, like adding -s in English
It means the word 'moon' and names the thing described
It marks the past tense of the whole sentence
panel.why: 很 is placed before an adjective in simple descriptions, and often does not mean "very" strongly.

teach.model: Colour words end in 色, such as 红色 for red. Shape words end in 形, such as 圆形 for a circle. To describe something, say the thing, then 是, the colour, and 的.

points.ask: What helps me spot a colour word?
And what about shapes?
How do I build a sentence?

trip.prompt: Find why red matters in Chinese festivals and name one place red is used.

stages.title: Family and people
stages.hook: Do you say the same word for an older brother and a younger brother? In Chinese you do not!
explain: Chinese family words show who is older and who is younger. 哥哥 (gēge) is older brother, 弟弟 (dìdi) is younger brother, 姐姐 (jiějie) is older sister, and 妹妹 (mèimei) is younger sister. 爸爸 is dad and 妈妈 is mum.

Grandparents also have different words. 爷爷 (yéye) is the father's father and 奶奶 (nǎinai) is the father's mother. For the mother's parents, people say 外公 and 外婆. Repeating a syllable often makes a friendly family word.
To say "my mum" you can say 我妈妈. With very close family, people often leave out 的. For a more distant thing, use 的: 我的书 (my book).
stages.mnemonic: Older siblings: gēge and jiějie; younger ones: dìdi and mèimei. The repeated syllable makes a friendly word.

gq.why: 妹妹 is a younger sister; 姐姐 is an older one.

gq.q: You have an older brother. What do you call him?

panel.q: Why does Chinese use different words for older and younger siblings?
o: Because the tones change depending on who is speaking
Because the words were chosen at random long ago
Because only boys are allowed to use these words
Age order is part of the relationship
panel.why: Age order matters in family relationships, and the language shows that respect.

panel.q: Which pair is father's side grandparents?
panel.why: 爷爷 and 奶奶 are paternal grandparents; 外公 and 外婆 are maternal.

panel.q: Why is 我妈妈 normally fine without 的?
o: Close family terms usually skip 的
panel.why: With close family, 的 is often left out, but 我的书 uses 的 for a thing.

teach.model: Chinese family words often show age order. An older brother is gēge and a younger one is dìdi. Grandparents also have words for dad's side and mum's side.

points.ask: Why are there two words for brother?
Which words are they?
What about grandparents?

trip.prompt: Find one way Chinese family titles differ from English ones.

stages.title: Common objects
stages.hook: Look around you. Can you name a pen, a bag and a door in Chinese?
explain: Each Chinese noun has a typical measure word. A book uses 本, a cup uses 个 (a cup of tea or water uses 杯), and a chair uses 把. For now, 个 (gè) is the most common measure word and can be used for many things.
The words 这 (zhè) this and 那 (nà) that help point to things. 这是书 means this is a book. To say there is something somewhere, use 有: 桌子上有一个杯子 means there is a cup on the table.
Many two-syllable nouns end in a light 子 (zi), such as 桌子 (table) and 椅子 (chair). This ending marks them as nouns and is said short and soft.
stages.mnemonic: Table 桌子, chair 椅子: little 子 at the end like a tiny child on a big thing.
sentences: There is a cup on the table.

gq.why: 这 is this, 是 is is, 书 is book.

gq.q: Which sentence means "There is a bag on the chair"?
gq.why: 上 means on and 有 means there is.

panel.q: Why do 桌子 and 椅子 both end with 子?
o: It is a common noun suffix
It means 'table' and is part of every noun
It shows the past tense when added to nouns
It means 'and' joining two objects together
panel.why: 子 is a common light noun ending in many two-syllable nouns.

panel.q: A shopkeeper asks 这是什么？ What are they asking?
panel.why: 什么 means what, so the question is "What is this?"

panel.q: Why is 一个 used in 一个球?
o: 个 is a general measure word
panel.why: Numbers need a measure word, and 个 is a general one.

teach.model: To point to a thing, say 这是 for this is and 那是 for that is. To say how many, put a measure word, like 个, between the number and the thing. Many nouns end in 子 such as 桌子.

points.ask: How do I say this and that?
What goes between the number and the noun?
What is the 子 on the end of table?

trip.prompt: Find examples of measure words and note two different ones.

stages.title: Everyday actions
stages.hook: Can you act out "eat", "drink" and "run"? Say the Chinese word as you move!
explain: Chinese verbs do not change for person or time. 吃 means eat for I, you or she. 我吃, 你吃 and 他吃 all use the same verb. Time is shown with extra words, such as 昨天 (yesterday), or small particles.
Basic order is subject + verb + object: 我吃米饭 (I eat rice), 他喝水 (he drinks water). To say something is happening now, put 在 (zài) before the verb: 小狗在跑 means the puppy is running.
Negatives use 不 (bù): 我不吃 means I do not eat. Questions can be made with 吗 (ma) at the end: 你吃吗？ means do you eat?
stages.mnemonic: Verbs never change dress: 吃 stays 吃 for every person.

gq.q: How do you say "I do not eat"?
Which word shows an action is happening now?
gq.why: 在 before a verb marks an action in progress.

panel.q: Why does 吃 stay the same in 我吃 and 他吃?
o: The tones of the verb change to show who is acting
Chinese verbs do not change for person
Only the pronoun changes the verb into a new form
It is always written twice, as 吃吃, to show the subject
panel.why: Chinese verbs do not conjugate for person.

panel.q: How can you make 你吃 a question?
panel.why: Add 吗 at the end of the statement.

panel.q: A friend says 我昨天吃米饭。 How is the past shown?
o: By the time word 昨天
panel.why: Time words like 昨天 show when the action happened, not a verb ending.

teach.model: A Chinese verb does not change form. 吃 means eat for everyone. You add 不 for no, 在 for happening now and 吗 to ask a question.

points.ask: How do I say not?
How do I say it is happening now?
How do I ask a yes or no question?

trip.prompt: Find how Chinese shows time without verb endings.

stages.title: Simple listening and speaking
stages.hook: If you do not understand someone, what can you say? These phrases are your lifeline.
explain: Useful classroom phrases help you keep a conversation going. 我不懂 (wǒ bù dǒng) means I do not understand. 请再说一遍 (qǐng zài shuō yí biàn) means please say it once more. 请说慢一点 (qǐng shuō màn yìdiǎn) means please speak a bit slower.
请 (qǐng) is a polite word for please. 请问 (qǐngwèn) is used to ask a question politely, like "excuse me, may I ask". 没关系 (méi guānxi) means it does not matter, which is a reply to an apology.
Listen for tones, not only for sounds. Practise by repeating after a speaker. Ask them to say it slowly and copy the rhythm. Even short answers like 好的 (hǎo de, okay) make you sound natural.
stages.mnemonic: Ask, listen, repeat: 请再说一遍!
sentences: I can speak a little Chinese.

gq.q: You did not understand. Which phrase helps?
gq.why: 我不懂 means I do not understand, which tells the speaker to help.

gq.q: Which word begins a polite question, like "may I ask"?
gq.why: 请问 is used to ask politely.

panel.q: Someone says 对不起 after stepping on your foot. What is a kind reply?
panel.why: 没关系 means it does not matter.

panel.q: Why should you listen to tone as well as sound?
panel.why: In Mandarin tone changes meaning, so tone is essential for understanding.

panel.q: Which is the best way to ask for repetition politely?
panel.why: 请 makes the request polite.

teach.model: If I do not understand, I can say wǒ bù dǒng, then ask the speaker to say it once more or to speak slower. Adding qǐng, which means please, makes it polite.

points.ask: What do I say if I do not understand?
Which word makes it polite?
What can I ask the speaker to do?

trip.prompt: Find a short audio sample of Mandarin and say it back slowly.
